notes: BATCH AJ (skin/scalp products: ichthammol, permethrin, dimeticone-lice, dexpanthenol, dexpanthenol-chlorhexidine, beta-sitosterol-beeswax, anti-haemorrhoid). All formulation routes are 'topical'. BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). Every quote checked FOUND with fetchtext --check. MHRA products SPCs were found through the MHRA products search index (mhraproducts4853.search.windows.net, the index products.mhra.gov.uk uses) and read from the MHRA document store. NO-UK-PRODUCT (4, after audit): dexpanthenol (no UK SmPC/PIL with dexpanthenol as the active substance for skin: emc 'dexpanthenol', 'bepanthen', 'panthenol'; MHRA products full-text 'dexpanthenol' only finds a xylometazoline/dexpanthenol nasal spray, a vitamin B syrup and products where it is an excipient); beta-sitosterol-beeswax (emc 'mebo', 'sitosterol', 'beta-sitosterol'; MHRA 'MEBO' 0, full-text 'sitosterol' only a saw palmetto THR and parenteral lipid emulsions); anti-haemorrhoid (clinic generic AND trade name are both 'Anti-Haemorrhoid', so the composition cannot be identified; the site monograph linked four UK SmPCs with two different compositions: emc 1470/1471 hydrocortisone acetate + bismuth subgallate/oxide + zinc oxide + benzyl benzoate + Peru balsam ointment/suppositories, and emc 1718/1599 hydrocortisone + cinchocaine ointment/suppositories; they have different contraindications (e.g. one says 'Do not use in pregnancy or breast-feeding'), so none was used; the integrator should get the ingredient list from the clinic pack and re-research). DIFFERENT UK PRODUCT USED (said in formulations[].note): ichthammol - only UK single-ingredient product is ichthammol 10% w/w in glycerol (liquid, chronic eczema), not an ointment or shampoo; permethrin - clinic product is a 1% shampoo, UK SPCs are a 1% creme rinse and a 1% cutaneous emulsion (the 5% cream is for scabies and was not used); dimeticone-lice - clinic 'Anti-Lice' shampoo (strength unknown), UK SmPCs are dimeticone 4% cutaneous solution (lotion left on 8 h); dexpanthenol-chlorhexidine - clinic product is dexpanthenol 5% + chlorhexidine 0.5% cream, the only UK match is a chlorhexidine dihydrochloride 0.5% w/w cream (Bayer) that lists 'Dexpanthenol' in 6.1 excipients (amount not stated). CONFLICTS (kept as separate items/rules): (1) permethrin age limits - creme rinse SPC: children 6 months and over, under 6 months not suitable except on a physician's advice, 6 months-3 years only under close specialist supervision; cutaneous emulsion SPC: adults and children over 3 years, not recommended under 3 years except on a doctor's advice. (2) permethrin breastfeeding - both SPCs: consider withholding treatment or temporarily stopping nursing; SPS: permethrin can be used in breastfeeding for PUBIC lice, and for HEAD lice wet combing or dimeticone are preferred (SPS does not give a head-lice recommendation for permethrin). (3) permethrin pregnancy - SPCs: avoid unless physically acting treatments failed and/or permethrin needed; BUMPS head-lice leaflet recommends wet combing first and lists physical insecticides (dimeticone) and malathion, not permethrin. NEW GROUPS: 'pyrethroid' (permethrin) used in the permethrin allergy rule; 'antiseptic' (dexpanthenol-chlorhexidine, povidone-iodine) used in the 'not concurrently with other antiseptics' rule - batch AL may add chlorhexidine-mouthwash to 'antiseptic' from its own SmPC. Source mhra-povidone-iodine-cream-pl58442-0003 is reused with the same id and URL as batch AH. NEW CONDITIONS: perforated-eardrum, compositae-allergy. Reused condition broken-ulcerated-skin (defined in batch AG). Head-lice products and medical devices: no UK source fetched here states that any of these clinic products is a medical device; the UK dimeticone 4% and permethrin 1% products used are licensed medicines (PL numbers), so nothing about device status was written. Dimeticone ingredient id is "dimeticone"; simeticone uses its own id "simeticone", so the duplicate check does not pair them. No brand-prescribing statement found in any UK source. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second check, see audit/AJ-AK-AL.md): dexpanthenol-chlorhexidine CONVERTED to no-uk-product (the UK chlorhexidine 0.5% cream has dexpanthenol only as an excipient; emc lists dexpanthenol as an active only in an IV multivitamin, a nasal spray and a vitamin B syrup), so its antiseptic group membership, the perforated-eardrum condition and sources emc-13700 and mhra-dsu-chlorhexidine-hypersensitivity-2012 were removed; the antiseptic group now has povidone-iodine only and no rule uses it. Ichthammol dose/paediatric items scoped to the ointment (not the shampoo). Breastfeeding/pregnancy info rules added (ichthammol, dimeticone-lice).
